text: Past medical history: Menarche at 13 years, regular menses every 28 days, lasting for 5 days. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Currently in a relationship with one male partner. Reports inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Pyelonephritis with likely concurrent Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID). The combination of high fever, elevated WBC, flank/abdominal pain, and a history of dysuria and dyspareunia in a sexually active young woman strongly suggests an upper urinary tract infection complicated by a pelvic infection. I recommend starting empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and arranging an urgent follow-up for urine culture and STI screening.
